=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:124-140 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: The failed-step extraction uses `last` while also matching `in_progress`, so it can select the diagnose step itself instead of the true root-cause failure.
  WHY: All reviewers identified the same regression; one review called it critical while others called it high, so the highest severity is kept.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-125 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq` is wrapped in `|| true`, which can hide API retrieval failures and leave `FAILED_STEP_JOBS_JSON` empty.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers reported the same masking behavior; the resulting empty JSON can still trigger downstream failure or fallback behavior.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:408-408 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `FIX_COUNT` is used in arithmetic without robust validation, so malformed or missing JSON can cause a shell arithmetic error or an early exit.
  WHY: Reviewers agreed this is a runtime robustness issue; severity is raised from the lower reports because one reviewer framed it as aborting the script under `set -euo pipefail`.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:443-443 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, google_gemini-3-flash-preview, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, stepfun_step-3_5-flash]
  PROBLEM: `sed 's/\\n/\n/g'` blindly converts literal `\n` sequences into newlines, corrupting issue bodies that intentionally contain escaped newline text.
  WHY: All reviewers agreed on the same content-corruption bug and gave high confidence.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:160-466 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3-flash-preview]
  PROBLEM: The script uses `sed -nE`, which may not be portable across all `sed` implementations.
  WHY: This was only reported by one reviewer and framed as a portability concern, so it remains a standalone low-severity finding.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-138 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Failed-step extraction uses `last` instead of `first`, misattributing failures to downstream steps instead of root cause.
  WHY: Diagnostic comments and fix-up issues will point to the wrong failed step, misleading debugging efforts.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:443-443 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `sed 's/\\n/\n/g'` blindly converts literal `\n` sequences to newlines, corrupting issue body content.
  WHY: Issue bodies containing literal backslash-n sequences, including code examples, will be corrupted.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:408-408 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `FIX_COUNT` should be validated as integer before arithmetic operations.
  WHY: The script could crash with an arithmetic error if JSON returns a non-numeric value.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-125 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq` failure masked by `|| true` could leave `FAILED_STEP_JOBS_JSON` empty with no fallback.
  WHY: The script might proceed without job data, though it has an `unknown-step` fallback.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:129-138 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq selector uses `last` on a result set that includes steps with `.status == "in_progress"`.
  WHY: Since the diagnose script itself is running from a step that is currently `in_progress`, `last` will often select the "Diagnose post-Codex failure" step instead of the earlier failed step that actually caused the workflow to stop. This misattributes the failure to the diagnostic tool in the final PR comment.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:408-408 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `FIX_COUNT` is used in arithmetic `seq 0 $((FIX_COUNT - 1))` without validating that it is a non-negative integer.
  WHY: If the LLM returns a malformed response where `fix_issues` is not an array, the `jq` fallback to `0` may fail or be bypassed if the type check is narrow; an empty or non-numeric `FIX_COUNT` will cause `seq` to throw a syntax error and terminate the script due to `set -e`.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-125 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `FAILED_STEP_JOBS_JSON` query uses `|| true` to mask failures from `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq`.
  WHY: If the GitHub API call fails, the variable is assigned an empty string. Downstream `printf '%s' "${FAILED_STEP_JOBS_JSON}" | jq ...` will then fail because an empty string is not valid JSON, and because the error is no longer masked by `|| true` on the `printf` line, the script will exit.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:443-443 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `sed 's/\\n/\n/g'` blindly converts every literal backslash-n sequence into a newline.
  WHY: Implementation fix-up issues often contain code snippets. If a suggested fix includes a string with a literal `\n`, this `sed` command will corrupt the code snippet by replacing the characters `\` and `n` with a physical newline, making the suggested fix syntactically incorrect or unreadable.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:160-466 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Uses `sed -nE` which is not portable across all `sed` implementations.
  WHY: While GitHub Actions runners typically use GNU sed, the repository's own utilities generally avoid `-E`; if this script is run in a different environment, the regex might fail to match, leaving `TRACKING_ISSUE_NUM` or `FIX_NUM` empty and breaking downstream issue cross-referencing.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3-flash-preview ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:126-140 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq query for extracting the failed step uses `last` instead of `first`, which can misidentify the diagnose step itself as the root cause.
  WHY: The diagnose step runs after the implementation step fails, and because it matches `status == "in_progress"`, `last` can select the diagnose step instead of the actual failure, causing incorrect root-cause attribution.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-140 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The jq query uses `last` to select from steps matching failure states plus `status == "in_progress"`, which can pick the diagnose step itself.
  WHY: When the diagnose step runs, it is actively in progress, so `last` may select it rather than the actual root-cause failure step, misleading diagnostic comments and fix-up issues.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:408-408 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `FIX_COUNT` is extracted from JSON and used directly in arithmetic without validation.
  WHY: If `jq` returns an unexpected value such as empty string, `null`, or malformed JSON, the arithmetic comparison will fail and the script will exit under `set -e`.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:421-421 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The body of each fix-up issue is passed through `sed 's/\\n/\n/g'`, which blindly converts literal `\n` sequences into actual newlines.
  WHY: Literal `\n` sequences in issue bodies, such as code examples, will be incorrectly converted and the rendered content will be corrupted.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:125-136 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq` call uses `|| true`, masking API failures.
  WHY: If the API call fails, `FAILED_STEP_JOBS_JSON` becomes empty and the script silently continues with `FAILED_STEP_NAME="unknown-step"` rather than reporting the diagnostic limitation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:124-130 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failed-step extraction uses `last` after selecting steps with `status == "in_progress"` alongside definitive failure conclusions.
  WHY: In a typical failure, earlier steps have `conclusion="failure"` and the current diagnose step has `status="in_progress"`, so `last` can attribute failure to the diagnose step itself and corrupt diagnostic metadata.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:408-408 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `FIX_COUNT` is assigned via `jq -r` without guarding against jq failure.
  WHY: With `set -euo pipefail`, a non-zero exit from `jq` aborts the script before fallback logic can run, preventing the deterministic fix-up issue path.
- `scripts/implement_diagnose_post_codex_failure.sh`:443-443 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The body of each fix-up issue is passed through `sed 's/\\n/\n/g'`, which blindly converts every literal `\n` sequence into an actual newline.
  WHY: `jq -r` already outputs raw strings with correct newlines applied, so converting remaining `\n` sequences alters the intended content and can break code snippets.
=== END FINDINGS FROM stepfun_step-3_5-flash ===
